tone_statements.citation: Diarra, Samassé & Nadezhda Makeeva. 2025. La formation du pluriel des noms en konabéré. Mandenkan 72: 129-179. doi:10.4000/15eo6
tone_statements.quote: Le tonème a une valeur phonémique en konabéré. Trois tonèmes unis s’opposent : haut (H), moyen (M) et bas (B). Sauf dans quelques cas particuliers, le ton n’est pas indiqué à l’écrit conformément à la politique orthographique mise en œuvre. Toutefois, la nature de cet article nécessite un marquage tonémique. À cet égard, le ton sera indiqué sur chaque lettre voyelle comme suit : á (H), ā (M), à (B). [...] Le ton moyen de la marque possessive n’influence pas celui du nom qui la suit, sauf si ce dernier est B-M ou commence par B-M. Dans ce cas, la séquence B-M est réalisée comme !M-M.
tone_statements.translation: The toneme has phonemic value in Konabéré. Three level tonemes contrast: high (H), mid (M) and low (B). Except in a few special cases, tone is not indicated in writing, in accordance with the orthographic policy in force. However, the nature of this article requires tone marking; tone will be indicated on each vowel letter as follows: á (H), ā (M), à (B). [...] The mid tone of the possessive marker does not influence that of the following noun, unless the latter is L-M or begins with L-M; in that case the sequence L-M is realised as !M-M.

tone_statements.citation: Wolthuis, Wilma M. C. 2019. Esquisse phonologique du bobo madaré nord (konabéré). Ouagadougou: SIL International (SIL WAF electronic publication; SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 81756). 39 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Nous avons identifié trois niveaux de tons phonémiques dans la langue bobo madaré nord : haut (H), moyen (M) et bas (B). [...] Bien que les trois tons soient évidents dans le système nominal, on n’en trouve que deux dans le système verbal. Ces deux tons correspondent en hauteur aux tons moyen et bas dans le système nominal. [...] il semble déjà qu’il y ait certains processus tonologiques qui ont un effet sur les tons lexicaux, comme l’abaissement tonal automatique (déclinaison, ‘downdrift’) et non-automatique (faille tonale, ‘downstep’), ainsi que le relèvement non-automatique (‘non-automatic upstep’) et la propagation de ton (‘spreading’).
tone_statements.translation: We have identified three phonemic tone levels in Northern Bobo Madaré: high (H), mid (M) and low (B). [...] Although the three tones are evident in the nominal system, only two are found in the verbal system. These two tones correspond in pitch to the mid and low tones of the nominal system. [...] it already seems that there are certain tonological processes that affect the lexical tones, such as automatic (declination, 'downdrift') and non-automatic (downstep) lowering, as well as non-automatic upstep and tone spreading.
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 levels (H, M, L) in nouns; 2 (M, L) in verbs; contour melodies; downstep

tone_statements.citation: Boone, C. J. L. (Carin). 2016. Tone in the Bobo Madare North Noun System. Master's thesis, Department of Linguistics, Leiden University (June 2016).
tone_statements.quote: Bobo Madare North has three contrastive level tones: high, mid and low (H, M, L). While this three-way contrast is evident in the noun system, only two contrastive tones are lexically present in the verb system. ... Thus each mora carries exactly one tone. I conclude therefore that the tone bearing unit in Bobo Madare North is the mora. Only level tones have been found on monomorphemic mono- and bimoraic nouns and verbs. ... Therefore I postulate that contour tones are sequences of level tones.
tone_statements.locator: Section 3.1 'Basic tones', p. 17 and section 3.3 'Tone bearing unit (TBU)', p. 22
tone_statements.summary: Three contrastive level tones H, M, L (verbs only M vs L) on the mora; contours are level sequences; automatic and non-automatic downstep after a floating L, tone spreading and occasional upstep.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Chapitre I 'Phonologie' (printed/pp. 5-10) covers vowels, consonants and 1.3 'Les tonèmes' (three level tones H/M/L, all contour combinations, plus a downstepped low); Chapitre II treats noun tone sandhi. No mention of stress/accent d'intensité anywhere; 'accent(s)' occurs only on p. 65 (13.13) meaning tone diacritics ('voyelles porteuses d'accents modulés').
